schema_basis.scope: Base entity fields plus relevant Location, Event, Collective, Institution, Object, Narrative, Language, Species, and Relation grouping vocabulary; SERVATI metadata is a local extension.

world_reference.note: The working pack supplied this root-world UUID but no corresponding entity. It is retained only for relational compatibility and must not be interpreted as canon.

entries.Name: The Pale Reef of Relay Twelve
entries.Description: A memory-centred continuity station whose cooling structure gradually became architecture, habitat, and sacred boundary. Its keepers treat quiet operation as proof of careful custody because vibration and signal noise once damaged fragile identity systems.

Setting.form: An archive habitat whose exposed heat-rejection ribs and accreted archive glass form one inhabited custody reef.
Setting.function: Preserve fragile identity relations under strict vibration and signal controls.

Construction.architecture: Occupied volumes follow the thermal ribs; every new enclosure must preserve cooling and evidentiary silence.

provenance.note: V11 provides an unnamed pale archive-reef Lamp with exposed radiator fins. Relay Twelve, its culture, and all other particulars are DRAFT V12 candidates.

servati.preservation_problem: The station must exchange heat and sometimes testimony without the vibration or signal noise its custodians believe can damage identity relations.
servati.editorial_notes: DRAFT candidate; not present as a verified named entity in the repository baseline.

entries.Name: The Ash Roads of Transfer Cluster K-6
entries.Description: A matter-first Lamp built through a mined asteroid. Burden movement remains physical and slow. Route gradients, resting thresholds, and load scars become the culture's most trusted historical evidence.

Setting.form: A custody settlement excavated through a dusty, low-gravity minor body, with burden roads cut along conservative load paths.
Setting.function: Move and preserve material burdens while retaining physical route evidence.

Construction.architecture: Road angles, rest shelves, and dust seals are kept as accumulated evidence rather than redesigned for speed.

provenance.note: V11 provides an unnamed dust-choked asteroid Lamp with burden routes cut through mineral ash. Cluster K-6, its culture, and all other particulars are DRAFT V12 candidates.

servati.preservation_problem: Every safer or faster alteration to a burden road risks erasing the load scars used to authenticate past transfers.
servati.editorial_notes: DRAFT candidate; not present as a verified named entity in the repository baseline.

entries.Name: The Drowned Threshold of Pelagic Vault Seven
entries.Description: A flooded custody complex whose inhabitants adapt to pressure, darkness, and submerged access. Here, approach is part of truth: a record removed from its depth, route, and threshold is considered dangerously incomplete.

Setting.form: A station above an ocean-bearing moon, connected to submerged vaults and coral-like preservation towers in dark water.
Setting.function: Keep records together with the pressure, current, depth, and approach conditions that give them relational meaning.

Construction.architecture: Pressure locks and tactile route surfaces make the path to a record part of the record.

provenance.note: V11 provides an unnamed Lamp above a drowned moon with black-water vaults, coral-like towers, and pressure-adapted custodians. Pelagic Vault Seven and all other particulars are DRAFT V12 candidates.

servati.preservation_problem: Moving a record may save its substrate while destroying the depth, current, and threshold relations that authenticate it.
servati.editorial_notes: DRAFT candidate; not present as a verified named entity in the repository baseline.

entries.Name: The Unopened Spring of Seed Reserve Thirty-One
entries.Description: A seed reserve whose activation rules outlive the civilisation that wrote them. Its culture grows around maintaining viability while debating whether any surviving authority can honestly declare the required future conditions satisfied.

Setting.form: A cryogenic reserve embedded in a cold-body service complex, surrounded by sealed trial ecologies and heat-management works.
Setting.function: Maintain viable developmental reserves while preserving release conditions no surviving authority can conclusively satisfy.

Construction.architecture: Nested sterile thresholds separate maintenance access, trial environments, and irreversible release access.

provenance.note: V11 provides an unnamed Seed Lamp keeping embryos viable after every release condition becomes obsolete. Reserve Thirty-One, its culture, and all other particulars are DRAFT V12 candidates.

servati.preservation_problem: Keeping the reserve closed preserves possibility but also consumes finite viability and may turn care into permanent non-release.
servati.editorial_notes: DRAFT candidate; not present as a verified named entity in the repository baseline.

entries.Name: The Corridor of No Arrival
entries.Description: A route-centred culture that continues maintaining a transfer corridor after its traffic disappears. Correct passage becomes the inheritance itself: markers are repaired, gradients checked, and receiving intervals opened even when nothing arrives.

Setting.form: A distributed chain of beacons, inspection refuges, and handoff points spanning an unverified interstellar route.
Setting.function: Maintain the possibility of lawful passage despite the loss of traffic and destination confirmation.

Construction.architecture: Habitats remain subordinate to beacon sight lines, maintenance paths, and receiving intervals.

provenance.note: V11 provides an unnamed route lamp maintaining beacons unused for longer than its recorded history. The Corridor of No Arrival, its culture, and all other particulars are DRAFT V12 candidates.

servati.preservation_problem: Changing an obsolete route could make it useful again but would sever the only surviving evidence of what its handoff sequence once protected.
servati.editorial_notes: DRAFT candidate; not present as a verified named entity in the repository baseline.

entries.Name: The Broken Frame Concordance at Transfer Site Nine
entries.Description: A rare mixed Lamp formed around a disaster site where damaged burden frames, partial names, and broken relation fields could not be reconciled honestly. Its keepers preserve fragments side by side rather than constructing a false single account.

Setting.form: A junction habitat built through a field of damaged burden frames and incomplete comparison machinery.
Setting.function: Keep material, memory, and pattern fragments mutually visible without forcing them into one false reconstruction.

Construction.architecture: Parallel galleries keep incompatible fragments within one comparison field while making uncertainty visible.

provenance.note: V11 separately provides damaged burden-capsule fragments and mixed sites vulnerable to division or purification. Their combination as Transfer Site Nine and all particulars are a DRAFT V12 synthesis.

servati.preservation_problem: The site must permit urgent use of fragments without allowing a useful reconstruction to overwrite the contradictions that make it honest.
servati.editorial_notes: DRAFT candidate; not present as a verified named entity in the repository baseline.

entries.Name: The Partition of Transfer Site Nine
entries.Description: Three custody authorities attempt to separate a mixed relic complex into matter, record, and pattern holdings. The Concordance refuses because the relations among the fragments are themselves evidence. The attempted partition damages the comparison field even though most physical material survives.

Nature.history: DRAFT event grounded in V11's description of mixed sites being divided, purified, or destroyed during the Custody Wars.
Nature.consequences: Becomes a candidate example of why preserving objects while severing relations can still constitute catastrophic loss.

relative_sequence.basis: DRAFT editorial ordering; Version 11 supplies no order among these examples.

provenance.note: V11 explicitly supports the mixed-site conflict type. Transfer Site Nine, the three authorities, actions, and consequences are DRAFT V12 particulars.

servati.preservation_problem: Separating the holdings may protect each substrate while destroying the comparison field that lets any of them correct the others.
servati.editorial_notes: DRAFT event; no chronology date is assigned.

entries.Name: The False Release at Seed Reserve Thirty-One
entries.Description: A release authorisation reaches the reserve carrying valid-looking procedural structure but incompatible provenance. One faction argues that delay is killing the future; another argues that activation under false authority would be irreversible violation.

Nature.history: DRAFT event combining V11's separate examples of a false release order and a seed reserve opened under one doctrine but mourned by another.
Nature.consequences: The reserve remains closed, but trust in remote authorisation collapses and later Seed communities require stronger plural verification.

relative_sequence.basis: DRAFT editorial ordering; Version 11 supplies no order among these examples.

provenance.note: V11 supports the two separate examples, not this combined incident. Reserve Thirty-One, its factions, outcome, and all other particulars remain DRAFT.

servati.preservation_problem: The reserve cannot both obey a possibly false command and retain the option to refuse it after activation.
servati.editorial_notes: DRAFT event; no chronology date is assigned.

entries.Name: The Silence Breach of Relay Twelve
entries.Description: An outside order forces a high-energy witness transmission through Relay Twelve, claiming that untransmitted identities are being abandoned. The local keepers argue the signal itself destabilises fragile relation fields.

Nature.history: DRAFT event combining V11's quiet-versus-resonant Lamp cultures with its later descriptions of forced access and data attack.
Nature.consequences: Some names are broadcast successfully; other uncertainty structures are damaged. Both sides preserve evidence supporting their accusation.

relative_sequence.basis: DRAFT editorial ordering; Version 11 supplies no order among these examples.

provenance.note: V11 supports the separate cultural contrast and war methods, but not a Relay Twelve incident. The transmission, actors, damage, and consequences remain DRAFT.

servati.preservation_problem: Broadcast may rescue unreachable witnesses while irreversibly disturbing the uncertainty structures by which their identities are compared.
servati.editorial_notes: DRAFT event; no chronology date is assigned.

entries.Name: The Redirection of the Ash Convoy
entries.Description: Two matter-custody orders claim the same convoy. Neither side wants to damage the burdens, so the conflict becomes a slow contest of route authority, frame control, and lawful handoff rather than conventional battle.

Nature.history: DRAFT event grounded in V11's example of opposing Pallbearer orders redirecting a sealed convoy without breaking vibration law.
Nature.consequences: The burdens survive, but their route provenance fractures into incompatible records that later communities cannot fully reconcile.

relative_sequence.basis: DRAFT editorial ordering; Version 11 supplies no order among these examples.

provenance.note: V11 explicitly supports the conflict type. The Ash Convoy name, orders, route dispute, outcome, and other particulars are DRAFT V12 candidates.

servati.preservation_problem: The burdens survive only if moved, yet every contested redirection weakens the route history needed to identify a lawful handoff.
servati.editorial_notes: DRAFT event; no chronology date is assigned.

entries.Name: The Drowned Marker Seizure
entries.Description: A rival authority removes submerged route markers from Pelagic Vault Seven, claiming the markers unlawfully bind later transfers to a dead spatial doctrine. Local custodians treat removal as destruction of historical relation.

Nature.history: DRAFT event grounded in V11's example of pressure-adapted custodians cutting drowned route markers from rival-claimed towers in reliquary coral seas.
Nature.consequences: The recovered markers survive physically, but their original currents, depths, and approach geometry cannot be recreated elsewhere.

relative_sequence.basis: DRAFT editorial ordering; Version 11 supplies no order among these examples.

provenance.note: V11 explicitly supports the conflict type. Pelagic Vault Seven, the seizure rationale, outcome, and other particulars are DRAFT V12 candidates.

servati.preservation_problem: A marker can be physically saved while losing the pressure, depth, and current relations that made its route testimony legible.
servati.editorial_notes: DRAFT event; no chronology date is assigned.

entries.Name: The Index Without Uncertainty
entries.Description: A copied identity archive is deliberately simplified so every record resolves to one answer. The copy is easier to use and spreads rapidly. Its missing uncertainty fields are discovered only after it has become the basis for transfers across multiple sites.

Nature.history: DRAFT event combining V11's separate examples of an archive copied without uncertainty fields and memory fields poisoned by false certainty.
Nature.consequences: Later custody decisions may be internally consistent but historically untrustworthy. No surviving authority can fully reconstruct which corrections were lost.

relative_sequence.basis: DRAFT editorial ordering; Version 11 supplies no order among these examples.

provenance.note: V11 supports the two separate examples, not this named multi-site incident. The deliberate simplification, spread, discovery, and consequences remain DRAFT.

servati.preservation_problem: The simplified copy is operationally useful, so preserving evidence of its omissions without allowing further use requires contradictory custody actions.
servati.editorial_notes: DRAFT event; no chronology date is assigned.
